findings.title: §4 threat model rows T-024-01/02/03 — invocation-log references are scenario-scoped, not normative per-slice deliverable claims
findings.evidence: T-024-01 (line 93): 'Cascade slice's invocation log captures target repo+branch BEFORE invocation, surfacing typos for review.' This is scoped to the wrong-adopter-misfire threat — an invocation scenario. It describes the log's audit function, not a normative requirement that all cascade slices must ship a log entry. T-024-02 (line 94): 'forensically detectable via the absence of invocation log entries' — this is about detecting unlogged credential-compromise invocations. It refers to the absence of log entries as a detection signal, not a mandate. T-024-03 (line 95): 'the cascade slice itself is still mergeable on the SCP repo because it ships only docs + invocation log entries' — this is explicitly the scenario where 'adopter-side maintainer rejects the wrapper PR AFTER cascade slice merges' (i.e., an invocation occurred before the rejection; this is NOT the `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` scenario where the conflict is discovered BEFORE invocation per T-024-10 + invariant 10). T-024-03 and T-024-10 are distinct threat rows covering distinct scenarios; T-024-03 accurately describes what a post-invocation-rejection slice ships. No propagation gap in §4 threat model.

findings.title: §5.6 Threshold A telemetry — companion sweep fix verified, line 185 scoped to Threshold A adopters
findings.evidence: §5.6 line 185: '≥3 of the 5 cohort adopters have `policy-check / scp/policy-check` required-check live + invocation log entries committed.' The `+` binds both conditions to the same ≥3 adopters counting toward Threshold A. Per §8 line 239, adopters with `cascade-status: blocked-on-adopter-conflict` do NOT count toward Threshold A's '≥3 of 5' criterion until a successor sub-slice onboards them. Therefore the '≥3 adopters ... + invocation log entries committed' is accurate: the only adopters that can form the ≥3 are `onboarded` or `onboarded-operator-bump`, both of which have invocation log entries per invariant 2. Line 187 carries the fix-round-5 companion sweep clarification: 'conflict-close slices have NO entry per invariant 2's negative assertion'. No propagation gap in §5.6.

findings.title: §6 slice plan rows 024C/024D/024E/024F unconditionally list 'invocation log' / 'invocation log entries' as deliverables — no conditional carve-out for blocked-on-adopter-conflict close-state
findings.evidence:
**§6 slice plan (plan-doc lines 202-205)** reads:

- Line 202: `| 024C | PIM cascade — adopter PR + SCP-side cascade slice + **invocation log** + post-bake observation | ...`
- Line 203: `| 024D | control-tower cascade — adopter PR + SCP-side cascade slice + **invocation log** + post-bake observation | ...`
- Line 204: `| 024E | mapp-doc-agent + recommender paired cascade — both adopter PRs + SCP-side cascade slice + **2 invocation log entries** + post-bake observations on both | ...`
- Line 205: `| 024F | shopify-app cascade — adopter PR + SCP-side cascade slice + **invocation log** + post-bake observation | ...`

In all four rows, the Deliverable column describes 'invocation log' or 'invocation log entries' as a mandatory component of the slice, with no carve-out for the `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` close-state.

This is the identical defect class as R4-NEW-MAJ-002 (§3 unconditional invocation-log claim) and R5-NEW-MAJ-001 (§1 item 2 unconditional invocation-log claim). Both prior rounds established this as MAJ severity for the following reason: a reader forming their model from §6 — the Slice plan, universally consulted by an implementor opening a new cascade slice — would conclude that 024C (for example) MUST ship 'adopter PR + SCP-side cascade slice + invocation log + post-bake observation'. If PIM has a pre-existing policy-check workflow conflict (T-024-10 scenario), the implementor would still include a log entry in the PR. This would trigger the CI negative-assertion check in `check-invocation-log-entry.sh` (invariant 2, `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` path: 'PR MUST NOT modify `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md`') and fail CI.

The inconsistency is directly verifiable:
- §1 item 2(b) (fixed at R5): 'conditional on the slice's `cascade-status:` declaration per §5.2 + invariant 2'
- §3 line 84 (fixed at R4): 'only when `cascade-status` is `onboarded` or `onboarded-operator-bump`'
- §5.2 line 133 (unchanged): 'only when `cascade-status: onboarded` or `onboarded-operator-bump`'
- Invariant 2 lines 44-47: explicit three-path model
- §6 lines 202-205: 'invocation log' — **no conditional**

Five of the relevant loci have the conditional; §6 does not. The pattern of propagation gaps across five rounds (R2 introduction → R3 §3+R-024-06 → R4 §3+§1 missed → R5 §1 caught → R6 §6 slice rows) demonstrates that §6 is the final propagation gap in this clause.

Note on 024E line 204: the unconditional '2 invocation log entries' is particularly misleading because it hard-codes a count (2) that assumes both mapp-doc-agent and recommender are on the `onboarded` or `onboarded-operator-bump` path. If one of the two has a conflict, the slice may produce 1 invocation log entry (or 0 if both conflict) rather than 2.
